sections.skill: Strategy: skip one square to find the opposite face
sections.relationship: Students try to picture the whole fold. The rule "in a straight row, squares with exactly one square between them are opposite" finds most opposite faces without folding in your head.
sections.author_note: Students try to picture the whole fold. The rule "in a straight row, squares with exactly one square between them are opposite" finds most opposite faces without folding in your head.

lesson.title: Skip one square to find the opposite face
text: A cube has 3 pairs of opposite faces. Opposite faces never share an edge.
In any straight row or column of the net, two squares with exactly one square between them end up opposite.
Squares that share an edge in the net always share an edge on the cube.
For a square sticking out of a row, slide it along its row in your mind: it is opposite the square two steps away along the direction it folds.

example.title: Worked example (a different net)
prompt: A net has the row 1, 2, 3, 4 with square 5 above square 2 and square 6 below square 3.
steps: In the row: 1 and 3 are opposite; 2 and 4 are opposite.
That leaves 5 and 6, which must be opposite each other.
Check: 5 touches 2 in the net, and 2 is not opposite 5. Every face has exactly one opposite.
